subtopics.title: The Multiple Access Problem
subtopics.summary: Why shared broadcast channels need coordination: when multiple nodes transmit at the same time, frames collide, all colliding frames are lost, and the channel is wasted during the collision interval.

subtopics.title: Channel Partitioning: TDM and FDM
subtopics.summary: Dividing the broadcast channel among nodes by time slots (TDM) or frequency bands (FDM) so each node gets a dedicated portion of the channel and collisions are avoided.

subtopics.title: Slotted ALOHA
subtopics.summary: The simplest random access protocol: time is divided into synchronized slots of one frame-transmission time, nodes transmit with probability p at slot beginnings, and colliding frames in a slot are all lost.

subtopics.title: CSMA and CSMA/CD
subtopics.summary: Improving random access with carrier sensing (transmit only when the channel is idle) and collision detection with backoff; the efficiency of CSMA/CD depends on the ratio of maximum propagation time to frame transmission time.

subtopics.title: Taking-Turns: Polling and Token Passing
subtopics.summary: Coordinating channel access by having a master node poll each node in round-robin fashion (polling) or by exchanging a control token that grants transmission rights (token passing).

subtopics.title: DOCSIS Cable Access
subtopics.summary: Case study of cable Internet access: the CMTS coordinates thousands of cable modems using FDM for downstream and upstream channels plus regulated upstream transmission, combining aspects of all three multiple access classes.
